subject.title: fix(cron): bound cron quarantine sidecar file reads

question: Should cron preserve write availability by creating recovery archives, and if so, what bounded retention or Doctor-managed cleanup contract should govern those archives?
rationale: The 8 MiB read/write bound is a narrow technical safety fix, but archive rotation changes persistent recovery-data lifecycle and disk-consumption behavior; tests cannot choose the product policy.

options.title: Keep the fix narrow
options.body: Remove archive rotation, restore the declaration contract, and land only the bounded read/write behavior so cap-exceeded writes remain an explicit failure.

options.title: Approve managed recovery archives
options.body: Keep rotation only after defining a bounded retention or Doctor cleanup flow, including user-visible diagnostics and validation of the cleanup contract.

options.title: Accept unbounded archives
options.body: Intentionally retain every recovery archive and document the resulting disk-growth responsibility for operators.

recommendation.title: Keep the fix narrow
recommendation.body: Remove archive rotation, restore the declaration contract, and land only the bounded read/write behavior so cap-exceeded writes remain an explicit failure.
